title: RGVisNet: A Hybrid Retrieval-Generation Neural Framework Towards Automatic Data Visualization Generation

problem.claim: Automatically generating data visualizations from natural language questions requires creating suitable specifications in declarative visualization languages.

gap.claim: Existing neural text-to-vis models generally generate visualizations from scratch, which limits performance because of the problem's complexity.

contributions.claim: RGVisNet is a hybrid retrieval-generation framework for text-to-vis that retrieves a relevant visualization query prototype and revises it to generate the desired query.

The retrieval model combines a schema-aware natural-language encoder with a graph-neural-network-based visualization-query encoder, while the revision model uses shared encoders and a visualization-grammar-aware decoder.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that RGVisNet is the first framework to integrate retrieval-based and generative-based approaches for the text-to-vis task.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On the public NVBench dataset, RGVisNet reportedly significantly outperforms existing generative text-to-vis models such as ncNet, with up to 74.28% relative improvement in overall accuracy.

narrative_sequence.summary: Data visualization systems help convey insights from massive data, and visualization requires specifications in declarative visualization languages.

The difficulty of mastering declarative visualization languages motivates natural-language-based automatic visualization generation, while existing from-scratch neural models face performance limitations.
RGVisNet retrieves a relevant visualization-query prototype and revises it using schema-aware, graph-based, and grammar-aware components.
The authors report improved overall accuracy on the public NVBench dataset relative to existing generative models.
The authors characterize RGVisNet as the first seamless integration of retrieval and generation for text-to-vis.

unknowns: The abstract does not describe the NVBench dataset size, data splits, baselines beyond the examples named, or statistical testing.
The abstract does not provide ablation results, implementation details, error analysis, or generalization beyond the reported dataset.
The abstract does not quantify the composition or coverage of the DV query codebase.
